diagnosis:
StarNet already has every part it needs. The problem is that most jobs have three to fifteen doors, and those doors go to different places and use different words.

**Output.** One WORKFLOWS job shows up in LAST JOBS, on the floor OUTBOX, in DELIVERABLES › TO REVIEW and in the library (windows/workflows.js:172,643,883; sidecar/index.js:16904). A new user's first chat output appears in none of the MY WORK tabs, because MY WORK opens on an empty TASKS board (stationui.js:1212-1213,4659-4665).

**Attention.** The rail NEEDS YOU and NOTIFICATIONS › NEEDS YOU read different sources, so their counts differ (needsyou.js:50-88 vs stationui.js:9392-9418). Pending builds, PROPOSALS and quest confirmations appear in neither list. Loop reviews and STEP-IN appear only in NOTIFICATIONS. The agent manual sends users to the other list (sidecar/manual.js:87,197,252).

**Vocabulary.** It drifts exactly where users get stuck:
- A scheduled job has about 7 names.
- "workflow", "loop" and "goal" each mean several things.
- The create screen still offers ASK FOR APPROVAL / FULL POWER (app.js:1787). Its ASK writes the LET IT WORK posture.
- The approval card and /yolo say "Full access" but only change approval mode (sidecar/index.js:2054-2060).

**Help and first-run copy.** They name doors that are hidden or wrong:
- The manual names CREW › RECRUIT and BUILD › CONNECT while the staged dock has them offline (systems.js:31,39).
- Model failures say "check CONNECT" (onboarding.js:953).
- Autonomy copy reads like an unlock ladder (nightreport.js:255-289).

**Verifiers corrected several premises:**
- Refusals already name their cause. The gap is four door labels that land unfocused, plus a RECONNECT that only navigates (friendlyerror.js:744-782).
- The desk stop was removed on purpose twice (418b3d95a, b0c57d5dc).
- Saving in SCHEDULES already turns the scheduler on (routines.js:798; sidecar/index.js:15590-15598). The INBOX form offers SAVE ONLY instead, so one action follows two rules, and the SCHEDULES status line wrongly says it won't run (routines.js:334).

**Top customer asks.** They line up with these seams: what pays for a run and why it stopped, how to connect a model, where to start, where files went, and where a key or control lives.

**The fix.** Nothing new needs inventing. The fix has five parts:
- Name one front door per job and point the other doors at it, keeping every capability.
- Use one word per concept.
- Fix a few defaults. Every default change is gated on Andrew's open calls.
- Put a one-line, truthful explanation at the exact spot each user gets blocked.
- Sequence the work after the in-flight final-* lanes (approval-truth, rc-seams, small-ports, customer-p1, build-ux) merge.
